title: The 5 Fastest Elevators on Earth, Ranked (Burj Khalifa Isn't on It)

scenes.text: The five fastest elevators on Earth. The Burj Khalifa doesn't make the list.
Number five: Two International Finance Centre, Hong Kong. About 10.6 metres a second, 38 kilometres an hour.
scenes.keywords: two international finance centre hong kong
scenes.label: Two IFC · 10.6 m/s

scenes.text: Number four: Yokohama Landmark Tower, Japan. 12.5 metres a second. The world's fastest from 1993 to 2004.
scenes.label: Yokohama Landmark · 12.5 m/s

scenes.text: Number three: Taipei 101. About 16.8 metres a second, over 60 kilometres an hour. Ground to the 89th floor in 37 seconds.
scenes.label: Taipei 101 · 16.8 m/s

scenes.text: Number two: Guangzhou CTF Finance Centre, China. 20 metres a second, and in a 2019 test it touched 21.
scenes.label: Guangzhou CTF · 20 m/s

scenes.text: Number one: Shanghai Tower. 20.5 metres a second, 74 kilometres an hour, in a pressurised cabin so your ears don't pop. The Burj Khalifa? Ten a second. Too slow.
scenes.label: Shanghai Tower · 20.5 m/s

description:
The five fastest passenger elevators in the world, ranked by rated speed.
Shanghai Tower's Mitsubishi Electric elevators run at 20.5 m/s (about 74 km/h), recognised as the world's fastest; Guangzhou CTF Finance Centre's Hitachi lifts are rated at 20 m/s and reached 21 m/s in a 2019 test; Taipei 101's Toshiba elevators (16.8 m/s) held the record from 2004 to 2016, and Yokohama Landmark Tower (12.5 m/s) before that. Two IFC in Hong Kong rounds out the five at about 10.6 m/s. The Burj Khalifa's elevators run at about 10 m/s.
Which of these would you ride first, and what should we rank next?
